subject: humanities
passage: Many illustrated manuscripts produced in the workshop of the Mughal emperor Akbar in the late sixteenth century carry small notes in their margins naming the artists involved. These notes frequently list more than one name for a single painting: one artist is credited with the design of the composition, another with the coloring, and occasionally a third with the faces. For art historians, the inscriptions complicate a habit inherited from the study of European painting, in which a work is attributed to a single master whose personal style it expresses. In Akbar's workshop, the notes suggest, a painting's distinctive qualities may have emerged from collaboration rather than from any one hand.
stem: According to the text, what do the notes in the margins of many manuscripts from Akbar's workshop indicate?

choices.A: Artists in Akbar's workshop, like European masters, were each credited with whole paintings.
choices.B: A single painting was often produced by several artists who handled different tasks.
choices.C: European painters had trained many of the artists who worked in Akbar's workshop.
choices.D: Every painting in Akbar's workshop was produced by at least three separate artists.

explanation.why: The text says the notes "frequently list more than one name for a single painting," with different artists credited for the design, the coloring, and "occasionally" the faces. So the notes show that paintings were often made by several artists with different jobs. Watch the qualifiers: "frequently" and "occasionally" rule out any choice that says "every."
explanation.A: Incorrect. The notes show the opposite: paintings were credited to more than one artist, which is why they complicate the European single-master habit.
explanation.B: Correct. This restates "more than one name for a single painting," with separate credits for design, coloring, and sometimes faces.
explanation.C: Incorrect. European painting is mentioned only as the source of art historians' habits, not as an influence on Akbar's artists.
explanation.D: Incorrect. A third artist is credited only "occasionally," and multiple names appear "frequently," not always.

checks.note: Best fit on the text alone.
